title: The unmarked finite-open-part functor is an etale algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes [def-weil-size-convention], and let $f:X\to Y$ be an $S$-morphism of schemes, separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Define a contravariant functor $P$ on $S$-schemes by letting $P(T)$ consist of pairs $(a,Z)$, where $a:T\to Y$ is an $S$-map and $Z\subseteq X\times_{Y,a}T$ is an open subscheme [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-open-immersion] whose projection to $T$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; restriction is pullback of the pair. This functor is an algebraic space $E$ over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]: there are natural bijections $E(T)\simeq P(T)$, with $E(T)$ its value as a sheaf. Forgetting $Z$ gives a morphism $p:E\to Y$ that is etale in the chartwise sense: for every representable etale chart $V\to E$ from a scheme, the composite $V\to Y$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. All schemes in an etale atlas of $E$ can be chosen in the chosen universe. No flatness or local finite presentation of $f$, section of $f$, separatedness of $p$, or scheme representability of $E$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 04QH (proposition-finite-algebraic-space), restricted to scheme source and target; equation-finite and lemma-finite-sheaf. Etale is chartwise, not an assertion that the morphism is representable.

proof.text: For an $S$-map $h:T'\to T$, set $(a,Z)|_{T'}=(ah,Z\times_TT')$. The fibre-product universal property identifies this with an open subscheme of $X\times_YT'$; open immersions and finite morphisms remain so after base change. Identity and composition of these restrictions follow from the canonical fibre-product identifications. Thus this is the stated presheaf $P$, with natural projection $p:P\to h_Y$. Apply finite-open-pair fppf descent to this exact presheaf to obtain its sheaf property.

Test the relative diagonal $P\to P\times_{h_Y}P$ on a scheme $T$ and two pairs $(a,Z_1),(a,Z_2)$. Apply the equality-locus lemma to $M=X\times_YT\to T$. It gives an open $V\subseteq T$ such that a map $T'\to T$ pulls the two pairs back equally exactly when it factors through $V$. This is precisely the functor represented by the diagonal pullback. Hence the relative diagonal is represented by open immersions. For two arbitrary pairs $(a_1,Z_1),(a_2,Z_2)$ on $T$, first impose $a_1=a_2$: the equalizer is the scheme $D=T\times_{Y\times_SY}Y$ via $(a_1,a_2)$ and the diagonal of $Y$. On $D$ impose equality of the two pulled-back opens by the same lemma. The resulting open subscheme of $D$ represents the absolute diagonal pullback. Thus the absolute diagonal of $P$ is representable by schemes.

source.place: Tag 04PK (lemma-finite-diagonal), proof and relative-to-absolute diagonal factorization.

proof.text: Choose the family $(a_i:U_i\to Y,W_i)$ of the finite-open geometric chart-family lemma, whose hypotheses are exactly the given separatedness and local finite type of $f$. The natural transformation $c_i:h_{U_i}\to P$ sends $h:T\to U_i$ to $(a_i h,h^*W_i)$; finite base change makes this a pair and the pullback identities prove naturality. For a test pair $(b,Z)$ on $T$, form $B=T\times_YU_i$. Pull $Z$ and $W_i$ back to $X\times_YB$; both are finite over $B$. The equality-locus lemma gives an open $B_i\subseteq B$ representing the subfunctor where they agree. Directly on sections, $B_i$ therefore represents $h_T\times_Ph_{U_i}$. Its projection to $T$ is an open immersion followed by the base change of the etale $a_i$, hence etale. This proves representable etaleness of every $c_i$, without presupposing algebraicity of $P$.

source.place: Tag 04QG (lemma-finite-surjective-etale-cover), construction of pairs, and Tag 04QE (lemma-finite-criterion-etale), scheme-test proof.

proof.text: Take the scheme coproduct $U=\coprod_{i\in I}U_i$, with the componentwise map $a:U\to Y$. The $c_i$ glue uniquely across its disjoint open components to a map $c:h_U\to P$: on any $T\to U$, the inverse images $T_i$ of the components form a disjoint open covering of $T$, the pulled-back pairs agree on their empty intersections, and the sheaf property of $P$ gives the unique pair on $T$. This construction commutes with restriction by uniqueness. On every test scheme $T\to P$, the pullback of $c$ is the scheme coproduct of the $B_i$ from step 3: maps into this coproduct are precisely disjoint open decompositions with component maps, and equality of pairs is checked on this open covering. Its projection to $T$ is etale since that holds on each open component. Likewise $a$ is etale by the source-local test. Both $I$ and the $U_i$ belong to $\mathcal U$, so their coproduct belongs to $\mathcal U$.

source.place: Tag 04QG (lemma-finite-surjective-etale-cover), disjoint union of the chosen scheme charts. Use the sheaf-gluing formulation, which does not require a separate finite-locality theorem.

proof.text: For each test scheme $T\to P$ and point $t\in T$, restrict its pair to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to T$. The chart-family lifting property supplies an index $i$, an extension $\kappa(t)\hookrightarrow L$, and a map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to U_i$ inducing that restricted pair after extension. By the section description in step 3 this gives a map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to B_i\subseteq T\times_PU$ whose image in $T$ is $t$. Every point $t$ is therefore in the image of $T\times_PU\to T$, so this projection is surjective. We have proved a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $c:h_U\to P$.

source.place: Tag 04QG (lemma-finite-surjective-etale-cover), geometric-point surjectivity argument and scheme-test definition of surjectivity.

proof.text: The sheaf $P$, its representable absolute diagonal, and the atlas just constructed satisfy the three defining conditions for an algebraic space. Let $E$ be this sheaf with that property; then $E(T)=P(T)$, naturally, and $p:E\to Y$ forgets $Z$. Regard $Y$ as its scheme algebraic space. The atlas composite $U\to E\to Y$ is $h_a:h_U\to h_Y$ for the etale scheme morphism $a$ of step 4; it is representable etale, since for every scheme $T\to Y$ the fibre product $h_T\times_{h_Y}h_U$ is represented by the scheme fibre product $T\times_YU$, whose projection to $T$ is the base change of the etale $a$, hence etale. Conversely, for a scheme chart $V\to E$ with $V\to E\to Y$ representable etale, testing on $\mathrm{id}_Y$ shows that the scheme morphism $V\to Y$ is etale. Source-atlas detection, clause (3), now implies that $p$ is chartwise etale: every representable etale scheme chart $V\to E$ has etale composite $V\to Y$. The atlas of step 4 is in the chosen universe. This proves all the positive assertions of the statement.
